subject: Private deployment commercial model: platform fee amortization & support tiers
messages:
From: Evan Moore <evan@skylinehealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on platform fee treatment + support tiers (Skyline RFP)

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the call this morning — the team is excited about Redwood's private deployment option. A couple of procurement / finance questions came up after reviewing the SOW:

1) Can the one-time platform fee be treated as a capital expenditure? Our accounting team prefers amortization over the contract term (we're looking at a 36-month window). If so, do you provide an itemized invoice we can attach to the CAPEX request?

2) Support tiers: your price sheet lists Standard, Enterprise, and Premium. Can you confirm which SLAs (response and on-call) are included in each tier and whether on-call blocks are additive or included with Premium?

3) Migration credit: we requested a migration credit in the SOW. Can you confirm the dollar amount and whether that credit is applied against the platform fee or monthly invoices?

I've attached the RFP excerpt and a short section our finance team flagged. Also looping in Nichols LLP (contracts) on potential billing language they might propose.

Appreciate quick clarifications — our internal budget deadline is 6/26, so if we can get firm answers this week, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Evan
---
Evan Moore
Director, Procurement
Skyline Health
[attachment: Skyline_RFP_SOW_v3.pdf (pdf)]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
To: Evan Moore <evan@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on platform fee treatment + support tiers (Skyline RFP)

Hi Evan —

Thanks for the clear list. Answers below at a high level; happy to jump on a quick call if you prefer.

1) Platform fee CAPEX: We can provide an itemized invoice that many customers capitalize. Redwood treats the platform fee as a one-time professional service / license line item on the invoice; your finance team can depreciate/amortize per your internal policy. We can also spread invoicing into up to 4 installments (e.g., deposit + quarterly draws) to help with cash flow; however, contractually the fee remains due per the payment schedule in the SOW.

2) Support tiers / SLAs:
- Standard: 9x5 email support, P1 response within 8 business hours, no guaranteed on-call.
- Enterprise: 24x7 on-call for P1 (response within 2 hours), 24x7 email for P2 with 8-hour response, quarterly healthchecks included.
- Premium: Enterprise SLA + named on-call roster, quarterly on-site or deep-ops review, priority routing for platform-level incidents.

On-call blocks are included with Premium (two dedicated on-call rotations for critical ops). For Enterprise, we bill on-call as an add-on in 4-hour blocks unless the customer purchases the Enterprise+ bundle.

3) Migration credit: As discussed in the commercial thread, we allocated a $75k migration credit tied to a minimum 36-month commit. Historically that credit is applied as a reduction against the platform fee on the final invoice. If you'd prefer it to offset monthly invoices instead, we can structure it as a monthly credit over 12 months — that would change how it impacts your CAPEX/OPEX treatment.

I've attached the Redwood price sheet for clarity. If Nichols has redlines on billing language, please send them along and we'll loop legal.

Next steps I propose: 1) confirm whether you want the migration credit amortized monthly or applied against the platform fee; 2) confirm preferred invoicing cadence (single invoice vs installments); 3) decide support tier and whether to include Enterprise on-call blocks. If you confirm by EOD Friday we can update the SOW.

Best,
Rachel

Rachel Kim
Senior Sales Director, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
[attachment: Redwood_PrivDeploy_PriceSheet_June2025.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Evan Moore <evan@skylinehealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Cc: Nichols LLP Contracts <contracts@nichols-llp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on platform fee treatment + support tiers (Skyline RFP)

Rachel — quick clarifications from finance & legal: 

- Finance prefers amortizing the platform fee over 36 months (helps our CAPEX approval). They asked whether Redwood can provide a single supporting invoice labeled "Platform license & deployment" with the $75k migration credit reflected as a line-item discount.
- Legal (Nichols) would prefer the migration credit applied to the platform fee (instead of monthly credits) — avoids having to reframe the payment schedule in the SOW. They may propose simple language: "Migration credit of $75,000 applied to the platform fee invoice upon successful handover."

Given that, we are leaning toward: amortize platform fee (customer-side), apply migration credit against platform fee, invoice in two installments (40% deposit, 60% on handover).

Can Redwood confirm we can get that invoice format and support language? Also, are there any discounts available if we commit to a 48-month term instead of 36?

Thanks,
Evan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Evan Moore <evan@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on platform fee treatment + support tiers (Skyline RFP)

Thanks Evan — appreciate the direction from your teams. Quick confirmations from our side: 

- Invoice format: yes, we can issue an itemized invoice that lists "Platform license & deployment" with a line for the migration credit as a negative line item. We'll include the SOW reference number and can mark the deposit vs final payment split.
- Language: the suggested Nichols wording is fine; we'll accept the proposed clause and will include it in the SOW redline.
- Term discount: for a 48-month commitment we can offer an additional 8% discount on recurring monthly fees (not the platform fee), or — if you prefer — a 6% reduction applied to the platform fee instead. Which would be more valuable to Skyline from a budgeting/tax perspective?

Also a heads-up on support: Enterprise on-call add-ons are frequently converted into the Enterprise+ bundle at renewal; if you select Premium now we can include a migration support playbook and two dedicated on-call rotations in the SOW. If you want the cost of Premium but plan to amortize platform fee, we can show both treatments on the invoice for your auditors.

I'll draft the SOW language and circulate a redline by Monday morning.

Cheers,
Marissa

Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Evan Moore <evan@skylinehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Cc: Nichols LLP Contracts <contracts@nichols-llp.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2025 15:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on platform fee treatment + support tiers (Skyline RFP)

Marissa / Rachel — thanks for the speedy answers and flexibility. Two final points before we move to signature: 

1) We'll take the 48-month commitment and prefer the 8% discount applied to recurring monthly fees (helps our operating forecast). Please reflect that in the pricing attachment and SOW.

2) Confirmed: migration credit to be shown as a line-item on the platform fee invoice; finance will amortize on their books. Invoice cadence: 40% deposit, 60% on handover.

Nichols: please go ahead and attach the brief redline we discussed.

If you can circulate the redline and final price sheet by end of day Wednesday, we'll route for internal signatures. Appreciate you both — looking forward to getting this across the line.

Best,
Evan

Director, Procurement
Skyline Health
